summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of coronary artery disease, systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and recent toe osteomyelitis, was admitted for evaluation of exertional and rest chest pain radiating to the jaw, associated with diaphoresis and gastrointestinal discomfort. Initial workup showed no EKG changes or troponin elevation. A cardiac catheterization revealed stable coronary disease without new blockages requiring intervention, leading to a diagnosis of unstable angina. He remained chest pain-free during the stay and was managed medically with continuation of anticoagulation, antiplatelet therapy, beta-blockade, and statin. His chronic foot issues, including a necrotic left toe ulcer and recent right toe disarticulation, were stable, and he continued a prescribed course of antibiotics for cellulitis. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with cardiology, podiatry, and primary care.
